notes:
107 stations: 36 changed, 71 unchanged.

How I set the years:
- Where Findlay 1887 gives an alteration year, the change falls in that year, and both the old and new spans include it.
- For undated changes after Edwards (March 1884), I used 1887 as the latest year. Findlay 1887 already carries 1887 alterations (Hasborough L.V., Flatholm), so the edition was compiled in early 1887.
- report1880's words often repeat report1879's, so a report may lag behind the light.

To check:
1. Revolving lights with colour sequences (Flamborough, Caernarvon Bay, Hartland, Owers, Wolf Rock, Point of Ayre IoM, Farne 1887). Findlay 1887 says outright that Hartland and Farne give 'a flash every 30 s / 20 s'. So the stated period is the interval between flashes, and a white-white-red cycle takes three times as long. Decide this before drawing.
2. Witnesses that contradict each other:
   - Outer Dowsing: report1879 says 90 s; Findlay says 20 s.
   - Leman & Ower: Findlay dates the change 1879, but report1880 still has the old two lights.
   - North Foreland: report1880 still says fixed in 1880, the change year.
   - Tees: white in the reports, red in Findlay 1887.
   - Owers: Findlay 1879 and Edwards have white-white-red; Findlay 1887 has white and red alternately.
   - St Agnes: Findlay 1879 says 1 min; everything else says ½ min.
   - South Stack fog light ('North Stack'): report1880 says 1½ min; Findlay 1887 says 1 min.
   - St Ann's Head Low: report1880 says red; Findlay and Edwards say white.
   - Point of Ayr (Flintshire): the red-sector bearings disagree.
3. Undated or doubtful changes:
   - Farne: the 20 s white-white-red came between 1884 and 1887.
   - Breaksea: the end of the red riding light rests only on Edwards leaving it out.
   - Flat Holm: occulting by 1884, then a second alteration in 1887.
   - Bishop Rock: Findlay says 1886; check against the new apparatus on the heightened tower.
   - Spurn high light, Plymouth Breakwater and Needles: occulting at some point 1879-84.
4. Alterations announced for summer 1887 (Royal Sovereign: triple flash every 45 s; Beachy Head: 4 s flash every 15 s) are not in the states. Both stations reported only in 1886.
5. Missing witnesses:
   - Casquets and Hanois: no Findlay entries (Channel Islands section).
   - Point of Ayr (Flintshire): no 1887 or Edwards witness, though the reports run to 1887.
   - Dee L.V.: only Findlay 1887 (1883).
6. Two-light stations where the keeper's tower matters: Happisburgh (low light given up 1884), Lowestoft (only the low light became occulting), Spurn, Dungeness, South Foreland, St Ann's, Nash.
7. Lights shown only some of the time: Berwick low (tidal), Bideford low (half-flood to half-ebb), South Stack fog light (fog only).
8. Light-vessel moves and sector changes that the keeper wouldn't see are recorded in what_changed but not counted as changes: Hasborough L.V. (1887), English & Welsh Grounds, Usk green sector, Nash red sectors, Landguard.
